big_case_rationale: Post-Jarkesy boundary case for agency adjudication of monetary penalties, with direct consequences for H-2A enforcement (a sixth of the agricultural workforce) and, by extension, other benefit-condition and employer-sanction schemes; a broad cross-ideological amicus field on both sides marks the stakes.

semantic_claims.proposition: The majority will rest the judgment on the absence of clear statutory authorization: 8 U.S.C. 1188(g)(2)'s grant of power to take actions 'including imposing appropriate penalties' authorizes the Secretary to assess monetary remedies but not to adjudicate them through binding in-house proceedings, reading 'impose' as FCC v. AT&T (2026) read the FCC's forfeiture power - assessment followed by court enforcement - and invoking constitutional avoidance because binding DOL adjudication of contract-based penalties and back wages would collide with SEC v. Jarkesy's claims-and-remedies analysis, while the Oceanic Steam immigration public-rights line is held not to reach employment-condition remedies covering domestic as well as H-2A workers.

The majority's stated ground will be narrow: confined to DOL's H-2A enforcement scheme under 8 U.S.C. 1188(g)(2) and to monetary remedies for employment-condition violations. The Court will not announce a categorical rule against administrative adjudication of civil penalties, will not overrule Atlas Roofing, and will expressly preserve executive adjudication of admission, exclusion, and other status-linked immigration matters, leaving DOL free to pursue the same remedies by suit in district court.
